reading.body:
One campus in Quincy, Washington discloses 36 MW of IT capacity, which is 60 percent of all data center power published for the state.

That share measures disclosure, not the state's actual footprint. Washington has 46 mapped facilities and only 2 with published capacity figures, so the true position of this campus within state data center load is unknown. The 60 percent figure is the best available number and it rests on a sample of two.

The physical numbers describe a high-density facility. At 720,000 square feet of technical space, 36 MW works out to about 50 watts per square foot. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the same load supports roughly 900 racks. Published specifications do not identify the tenant mix or workload type, so nothing here establishes how much of that capacity serves AI training rather than other compute.

What the data does not cover is the part that decides whether this campus matters for AI scaling. No certifications or utility partnership details are published. It does not say whether 36 MW is current draw or available headroom, whether the grid connection can support expansion, or whether the operator has filed for capacity beyond what is disclosed. The suitability score of 68 names announced expansion as its missing input, which is the same gap.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
